top_stories.title: Trump dangles normalisation amid pro-Israel criticism of possible Iran deal | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **President Donald Trump** is pushing for regional countries to establish formal diplomatic relations with Israel as part of a potential peace deal with **Iran**.  Some pro-Israel politicians, including **Senator Lindsey Graham**, have softened their stance on the Iran deal in light of this push.  However, critics like **Senator Ted Cruz** and former Secretary of State **Mike Pompeo** express concerns about the proposed deal, arguing that it would not effectively address Iranian threats to US allies. The Trump administration has defended its approach, dismissing criticism as uninformed.

top_stories.title: President Sheinbaum allows Iran team to stay in Mexico during World Cup after US refusal | Claudia Sheinbaum | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Claudia Sheinbaum**, Mexico's president, announced that the **Iranian national football team** will be allowed to stay in Mexico during the World Cup after **Fifa** approached her government following a refusal from the **United States**.  The decision was made to avoid visa complications and allow for direct travel to Mexico by **Iran Air** flights. The Iranian team's base will now be located in Tijuana, Mexico.

top_stories.title: Ex-Scottish National Party chief pleads guilty to embezzling funds | Politics News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Peter Murrell**, former chief executive of the **Scottish National Party (SNP)**, pleaded guilty to embezzling over 400,000 British pounds from the party's funds.  Murrell admitted the offences at the High Court in Edinburgh after a years-long investigation into the SNP’s finances and alleged diversion of donations intended for Scottish independence. The judge remanded Murrell in custody before sentencing on June 23rd, while **John Swinney**, current First Minister of Scotland, expressed his betrayal by Murrell's actions.

top_stories.title: Horse trading at horse speed: DMK chief Stalin on AIADMK MLAs joining TVK - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **DMK** president M.K. Stalin criticized the resignation of three **AIADMK** MLAs and their subsequent meeting with Minister **Aadhav Arjuna** at the Secretariat to join the **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)**, calling it "horse trading."  **R.S. Bharathi**, DMK organization secretary, accused the TVK of using social media for false propaganda regarding a rape and murder case in Sulur, Coimbatore. **Anbumani Ramadoss**, PMK president, questioned the motives behind the resignations, suggesting they were driven by power-seeking rather than genuine political concerns. Former VCK MLA S.S. Balaji deemed the actions unethical and a threat to the TVK's claim of clean politics.

top_stories.title: Israel to intensify Lebanon offensive in bid to ‘crush’ Hezbollah | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Benjamin Netanyahu**, the Israeli Prime Minister, ordered an intensification of strikes against **Hezbollah** in Lebanon to "crush" the armed group. The order came despite a ceasefire agreement with Lebanon last month and amid daily strikes on southern Lebanon.  The escalation was met with an exodus from Beirut's southern suburbs, a major Hezbollah stronghold. **Netanyahu** stated that Israel would not be taking its "foot off the gas," while **Hezbollah** has been blamed for attacks using explosive drones. The Israeli military reported a soldier killed by a drone strike and another severely injured in southern Lebanon.

top_stories.title: More than 1.5m foreign pilgrims begin Hajj despite Iran war fears
top_stories.rephrased_article: Over 1.5 million foreign pilgrims have begun the annual Hajj pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia despite concerns about the ongoing conflict between the US, Israel, and Iran. **Saudi authorities** reported a slight increase in pilgrim numbers compared to last year, with many expressing hope for peace between the warring nations.  The pilgrimage is one of Islam's five pillars and involves various rituals at sacred sites throughout Mecca and Medina.

top_stories.title: Starmer urged to intervene in ‘rigged’ Indian prosecution of British human rights activist | India | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Keir Starmer**, as a former human rights lawyer, has been urged by four senior lawyers, including **Dominic Grieve**, to intervene and request that Indian prosecutors drop charges against British national Jagtar Singh Johal. The letter argues that continued prosecution would violate the double jeopardy rule, which prevents someone from being tried twice for the same offense.  The letter cites international law and domestic legal systems around the world as supporting this argument. It also highlights the UN's finding that Johal is arbitrarily detained due to his activism exposing human rights abuses against India's Sikh community.

top_stories.title: Tim Hortons says it will hire 10,000 locals in Canada amid boycott call, 'Singh Hortons' nickname - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Tim Hortons**, the restaurant chain, announced a shift away from its reliance on **Temporary Foreign Worker** (TFW) programs and will prioritize hiring 10,000 local workers as it expands across Canada.  The company's parent company, **Restaurant Brands**, stated that they have not lobbied for TFW program changes and are committed to hiring locally. The spokesperson clarified that the wage structure is consistent for all employees and that there was never a preference for cheap labor.

top_stories.title: Czech police detain Russian priest over ‘white substance’ find | Crime News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Czech** police detained a Russian Orthodox priest, Bishop Hilarion, after discovering four containers of a suspicious white substance in his car. **Moscow** condemned the detention as an "orchestrated provocation" and demanded his immediate release. The **Russian Foreign Ministry** spokeswoman called the incident unacceptable high-handedness by the Czech authorities.  Hilarion denied any involvement in drug possession and claimed he was not given clear reasons for the police stop.

top_stories.title: Benjamin Netanyahu says Israel will intensify strikes against Hezbollah
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Benjamin Netanyahu**, the Israeli Prime Minister, announced a renewed offensive against **Hezbollah** in Lebanon. The **Israel Defense Forces (IDF)** launched strikes across the country, targeting Hezbollah sites in the Bekaa Valley and other areas. This escalation follows a ceasefire agreement signed earlier this month, but fears persist that the attacks could expand to include Beirut.  The Iranian government has called for a complete ceasefire as part of any peace deal with the US.
